requirement:
TOML reports only `Comment` attachments. Each `#` comment is one attachment,
including a comment following a value on the same line. A `#` inside a quoted
string belongs to the string.
rationale:
The `test.toml` case in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` covers each clause of `requirements.sdk.sources.toml.attachments`. The test carries a `{test}` reference to the requirement.

The `test.toml` input is `# first\n# second\na = '# literal' # real\n"# key" = """# literal"""`. The expected attachments are `(Comment, "# first")`, `(Comment, "# second")` and `(Comment, "# real")`.

- **Only `Comment` attachments, each `#` comment its own attachment.** `# first` and `# second` are adjacent comment lines. The test expects two separate attachments, not one merged attachment. The assertion compares each attachment's kind and its exact source text. A merged attachment or a wrongly classified kind would fail it.
- **A comment following a value on the same line.** `a = '# literal' # real` yields a separate `# real` comment. The assertion checks that exact text.
- **A `#` inside a quoted string belongs to the string.** Three cases are checked, and none of them may produce an attachment:
  - the single-quoted literal string `'# literal'`;
  - the double-quoted basic string used as a key, `"# key"`;
  - the multi-line basic string `"""# literal"""`.
  The assertion compares the full list of found attachments, so any spurious comment from these strings would make it fail.

Two inputs are not tested directly: a double-quoted basic string used as a value, and a multi-line literal string written with `'''`. These fall in classes already represented. The quoted key uses the same basic-string syntax as a basic-string value, and the multi-line basic string covers the multi-line form. I count them as further values within represented classes, not gaps.

No `Annotation` appears for TOML, which matches the "only `Comment`" clause. The assertion compares the whole attachment list, so any extra attachment of another kind would also fail it.
